newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Matos sees fiscal surplus in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Matos sees fiscal surplus in 1997.

text.p: The Venezuelan government will record a fiscal surplus equivalent to at least one percent of the country's gross domestic product in 1997, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said Tuesday.
"The government will report a surplus greater than one percent," Matos told reporters in Congress.
Matos added that for the current fiscal year the government expects to at least break even.
"In 1996, we are going to end in balance or with a small surplus," he said.

The finance minister recalled that in 1995 the government had a fiscal deficit equivalent to 7.5 percent of GDP and insisted that the dramatic recovery was thanks to the government's economic reform program launched in April.
Independent analysts, however, have said the improvement in fiscal accounts was due mainly to higher-than-expected oil revenues from strong oil prices in the second half of the year.
Matos said Venezuela was now in a comfortable fiscal position and would not need to raise taxes.
Indeed, if the government continues to run a fiscal surplus in coming years, "it could mean that the government will revise its taxation policy," he added.
